question: A report cites a locally present BLOB where a Landed commit is required. The object exists, so the citation is resolvable and its type is known: it is not a commit. That is a real failed finding (exit 1), never an uncertain missing (exit 2).

fixture.lane: one commit 'round-1: work' by kama-shokunin at author time 1000; file 'f' whose blob sha T is the wrong-type citation target
fixture.fleet: commit 'round-1: report' at author time 2000 adding .ufo/reports/round-1/kama.md
fixture.report: ## Landed changes cites the real lane commit LC (40-hex) and the blob sha T (40-hex); no other hex token
fixture.blob_target: T = sha1 of the lane file blob; cat-file -t T == blob; T^{commit} does not peel

arms.full: plain offline clone of the origins; no promisor metadata at all
arms.promisor-metadata: same content, plus promisor metadata only: core.repositoryformatversion=1, remote.origin.promisor=true, remote.origin.partialclonefilter=blob:none; every object already present locally; remote.origin.url is a local path

fixture.offline: no network transport, no remote command, no credential helper, no core.sshCommand; the only remote URL is a local filesystem path

full.rationale: T exists in the lane, so the full-hash existence scan resolves it; only the Landed commit requirement fails. Exactly one defect.

promisor-metadata.rationale: Same substantive finding as the full clone: promisor metadata alone does not establish incompleteness, and a present wrong-type object is proved evidence, not an unknown.

amendments.added_after: the builder existed; expectation unchanged, arms added for coverage

promisor-lane-only.rationale: Only the lane carries the metadata; the citation still resolves locally in the lane, so the finding must stand.

promisor-fleet-only.rationale: Only the fleet carries the metadata; the cited blob is in the lane and present, so the finding must stand.

non-promisor-unrelated-hole.rationale: An unrelated missing blob (referenced by a post-report tree, deleted from the store, cited nowhere) must not change the verdict. Measured at base: exit 1 with exactly this one defect, so the expectation is anchored, not guessed.

promisor-metadata-unrelated-hole.rationale: Same as the row above with promisor metadata on both repositories: an unrelated hole is still unrelated. Kills an 'any hole means unknown' rule applied to peel failures.

frozen_base_measured.note: the r23 refusal precedes any content check

amendments.peer_row_note: Peer OracleLocalBlobType built the same shape as its P10/P10b with a different fixture token 4c226b603e6a26a14212b131fcac232ca7318852. That token belongs to the peer fixture; it must stay apart from T=6e98d181389d343031fd578c6a775ce0889a8b0d in every expectations file.
amendments.mechanism_correction: Landed-span tokens are ALWAYS in the full-hash scan: without corpus/SOURCES.md, classify_full_hashes returns FULL.findall(text) over the whole report (tools/report-landing-audit.py:285); with SOURCES.md, :293 (lo <= start < hi) puts every Landed-span token INTO the scanned set, and only an exact Registry-URL occurrence outside the Landed span is diverted to 'classified'. Therefore T is seen by BOTH lookups in this cell: the no-peel lookup resolves it (the blob is present) and the peel to a commit fails, which is what yields the single defect. The absence of unresolved-full-hash here is therefore NOT a Landed-span exclusion effect, and the expectation must not be written as SOURCES-dependent.

full.note: base already reports the wrong-type citation as a failed finding

promisor-metadata.note: base refuses any promisor-marked repository before looking at content; this is the r23 harm

candidate_requirement: promisor-metadata arm must reach the same exit and the same defect kinds as the full arm; exit 2 (could-not-evaluate) on this cell is a regression of the r23 harm, and an extra unresolved-full-hash defect (blob not found) is a second regression: the object is present.
